acceptance_criteria.criterion: Running node scripts/extract-dialogue.js <chunk-file> produces a .md file in the same directory as the source .jsonl, with the same base name
The .md file contains only assembled prose text from AI turns — no tool call JSON, no tool results — one paragraph block per AI turn
For single-namespace chunk files, the output is flat prose without section headers
For dual-namespace chunk files, the output has ## Outer Agent and ## Inner Agent section headers
Running the script on a directory extracts all *.jsonl files in that directory (non-recursive, sorted alphabetically)
Running with --dry-run prints the output paths without writing any files
An existing .md file is not overwritten unless --force is passed
Running with --help or -h displays usage information and exits
node scripts/cli.js extract-dialogue <args> invokes the script correctly
The COMMANDS entry uses key: null, helpHidden: true, and category: 'Orchestrator' — matching the read-log pattern

summary: Created scripts/extract-dialogue.js — a stdlib-only Node.js ESM CLI script that extracts prose text from LangGraph agent chunk .jsonl files.
Implemented parseArgs(), discoverChunkFiles(), parseJsonl(), assembleText(), extractFile(), and main() following the read-log.js pattern.
Single-namespace output produces flat prose; dual-namespace (outer and inner both populated) produces ## Outer Agent / ## Inner Agent headers.
Supports --force (overwrite), --dry-run (preview paths), --help/-h (usage), positional arg or --file/--dir flags.
Added cmdExtractDialogue() function to scripts/cli.js and a COMMANDS array entry immediately after read-log with key: null, helpHidden: true, category: 'Orchestrator'.
All acceptance criteria verified manually against real .jsonl chunk files from the storage ledger.

comments.note: scripts/extract-dialogue.js implements its own JSONL chunk parser from scratch (stdlib-only by design) while chunk-accumulator.ts/chunk-renderer.ts provide the same logic in TypeScript. This is intentional per the WP spec ('independent pure-JS implementation avoids build coupling'). However, any future evolution of the chunk format must be reflected in both places independently — worth noting in the codebase docs.

scripts/read-log.js uses individual named imports (import fs from 'fs'; import path from 'path') but the shebang line convention is consistent. The new extract-dialogue.js follows the same pattern identically.

The assembleText() function accumulates outer vs inner namespace by ns.length: 0 = outer, >0 = inner. This is a simplification — in practice, a file could have multiple inner namespaces (e.g. pm:..., developer:...) all merged together. A more fine-grained implementation could separate each named namespace, but the dual-section spec only distinguishes two levels, so this is correct by spec.

summary: Reviewed scripts/extract-dialogue.js and the extract-dialogue COMMANDS entry and cmdExtractDialogue() function in scripts/cli.js.

Implementation faithfully mirrors read-log.js in every structural dimension: shebang, stdlib-only ESM imports, WORKSPACE_ROOT derivation, USE_COLOR / C object, HELP constant, section comment style, parseArgs() pattern, and main() structure.

parseArgs() arg-consumption logic for unknown flags is correct: the speculative ++i / i-- undo pattern handles --flag val forms safely, and the eq !== -1 branch (--flag=val) never speculatively increments i so no undo is needed.

assembleText() binary bucket logic (outer = ns.length === 0, inner = ns.length > 0) is spec-correct for the two-level dual-namespace requirement. Developer's own note acknowledges the multi-namespace simplification — appropriate for current spec.

extractFile() status return 'empty' is internally consistent: a placeholder file IS written and main() increments the empties counter. The summary line in non-dry-run mode emits '1 empty' without clarifying the file was created. No functional bug — flagged as low-priority improvement.
discoverChunkFiles() silently swallows readdirSync errors. Acceptable UX tradeoff (user sees 'No .jsonl files found') but loses the underlying error detail. Low-priority.
Double path resolution in main() (existence check + discoverChunkFiles internal resolve) is a minor inefficiency, not a bug. Not Fix-Forward-eligible without a function signature change.
cli.js COMMANDS entry: key: null, helpHidden: true, category: 'Orchestrator' — exact match to read-log pattern. Positioned correctly immediately after the read-log entry.
No blocking issues found. No Fix-Forward edits applied. Documentation-forward item identified for the chunk-format divergence note.

comments.note: extractFile() returns status: 'empty' when it writes the placeholder '*No dialogue recorded.*' — a file IS created on disk, but main() counts it separately from 'written'. The summary line emits e.g. '1 empty' without clarifying a file was written. Consider changing the summary label to '1 empty (written)' or folding empties into the written count with a parenthetical note, so users do not assume no output was produced.

discoverChunkFiles() catches readdirSync errors and returns [] silently. This causes main() to emit 'No .jsonl files found.' when a permissions error occurs on the directory, losing the original OS error. A future improvement could distinguish 'directory not readable' from 'directory is empty' — though the current UX is acceptable for the tool's intended use context.

main() resolves opts.target to an absolute path for the existence check (lines 415-417), then passes the original opts.target to discoverChunkFiles(), which resolves it again internally. Both paths produce the same result and there is no bug, but passing the already-resolved path to discoverChunkFiles() would eliminate the redundant resolve call and make the function's input invariants clearer.

[documentation-forward] scripts/extract-dialogue.js is an intentional parallel implementation of the chunk parsing logic that also exists in chunk-accumulator.ts and chunk-renderer.ts (TypeScript). This divergence is correct by design (stdlib-only, no build coupling), but it is not documented in the codebase. The README or a CONTRIBUTING/SCRIPTS.md should note that any evolution of the chunk format must be reflected in both places independently — the scripts/ directory carries its own parser that is not derived from the TypeScript source.
